content: Diprobase is an emollient specifically designed for the management of eczema and dermatitis. It functions as an occlusive emollient, meaning it helps to restore the natural oil layer on the skin's surface, thereby reducing water loss. This mechanism of action can result in a sticky sensation on the area where it is applied. Diprobase does not contain any pharmacologically active ingredients. Its formulation consists of a combination of paraffins and water, along with cetomacrogol and cetostearyl alcohol, which act as emulsifying agents. Additionally, it includes chlorocresol, which serves as an antimicrobial preservative, as well as phosphoric acid and sodium dihydrogen phosphate. Dry skin occurs due to a deficiency of water in the outermost layer of the skin, known as the stratum corneum. When this layer becomes dehydrated, it loses its elasticity, leading to cracking, scaling, and sometimes itching. The stratum corneum naturally contains substances that hold water, which is drawn up from the deeper layers of the skin. Normally, water is retained in this layer by a surface film composed of natural oils (sebum) and broken-down skin cells, which act to slow the evaporation of water from the skin's surface. Diprobase enhances this protective oil layer, thereby improving the skin's ability to retain moisture.
